title: Exact and fuzzy duplicates; record matching

videos.script: Some duplicates are easy. The same row, twice, byte for byte. One line of code removes them. {{exact}} The hard ones are the same person under two accounts. Mariana signed up in the shop, and a year later in the app. Her name has lost its accent. Her postcode has lost its hyphen. {{person}} Matching them takes three steps. Bring every field to a plain form. Measure how alike two names are. And only compare records that share something, or you will be comparing millions of pairs. {{steps}} Then comes the decision. Two records with the same name are often two different people. Two hundred and fifty-nine times in this file. {{homonyms}} Because the lab knows which records really are the same person, every rule in this lesson gets a score. Right matches, wrong matches, and the ones it missed. {{score}} And merging is its own decision. Which record survives, which values it keeps, and what happens to the orders that pointed at the other one. {{end}}
